arxiv-1611-04038.title: Laser Pulsing in Linear Compton Scattering
arxiv-1611-04038.creator: G. A. Krafft 1,2 , E. Johnson 1 , K. Deitrick 1 , B. Terzić 1 , R. Kelmar 3 , T. Hodges 4 , W. Melnitchouk 2 , J. R. Delayen 1,2
arxiv-1611-04038.description: Abstract Previous work on calculating energy spectra from Compton scattering events has either neglected considering the pulsed structure of the incident laser beam, or has calculated these effects in an approximate way subject to criticism. In this paper, this problem has been reconsidered within a linear plane wave model for the incident laser beam.

arxiv-2202-05986.title: Outstanding thermoelectric performance predicted for out-of-plane p-doped GeSe
arxiv-2202-05986.creator: Anderson S. Chaves, Daniel T. Larson, Efthimios Kaxiras, Alex Antonelli
arxiv-2202-05986.description: Abstract The record-breaking thermoelectric performance of tin selenide (SnSe) has motivated the investigation of analogue compounds with the same structure. A promising candidate that emerged recently is germanium selenide (GeSe). Here, using extensive first-principles calculations of the hole-phonon and hole-impurity scattering, we investigate the thermoelectric transport properties of the orthorhombic phase of p-doped GeSe.

arxiv-2210-11627.title: Obvious manipulations of tops-only voting rules Thanks: We thank Jordi Massó for his very detailed comments. We acknowledge financial support from UNSL through grants 032016, 030120, and 030320, from Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas (CONICET) through grant PIP 112-200801-00
arxiv-2210-11627.creator: R. Pablo Arribillaga, Agustín G. Bonifacio
arxiv-2210-11627.description: Abstract In a voting problem with a finite set of alternatives to choose from, we study the manipulation of tops-only rules. Since all non-dictatorial (onto) voting rules are manipulable when there are more than two alternatives and all preferences are allowed, we look for rules in which manipulations are not obvious.

arxiv-2306-05442.title: FlowFormer: A Transformer Architecture and Its Masked Cost Volume Autoencoding for Optical Flow Thanks: Zhaoyang Huang and Xiaoyu Shi assert equal contributions, Zhaoyang Huang, Xiaoyu Shi, Xiaogang Wang, and Hongsheng Li are with the Department of Electronic Engineering, The Chinese University of H
arxiv-2306-05442.creator: Zhaoyang Huang*, Xiaoyu Shi*, Chao Zhang, Qiang Wang, Yijin Li, Hongwei Qin
arxiv-2306-05442.description: Abstract This paper introduces a novel transformer-based network architecture, FlowFormer, along with the Masked Cost Volume AutoEncoding (MCVA) for pretraining it to tackle the problem of optical flow estimation. FlowFormer tokenizes the 4D cost-volume built from the source-target image pair and iteratively refines flow estimation with a cost-volume encoder-decoder architecture.

arxiv-2309-01294.description: Abstract In the past few years, AlphaZero’s exceptional capability in mastering intricate board games has garnered considerable interest. Initially designed for the game of Go, this revolutionary algorithm merges deep learning techniques with the Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS) to surpass earlier top-tier methods.

arxiv-2404-07535.title: Free boundary regularity for the inhomogeneous one-phase Stefan problem
arxiv-2404-07535.creator: Fausto Ferrari, Nicolò Forcillo, Davide Giovagnoli, David Jesus
arxiv-2404-07535.description: Abstract Abstract. In this paper, we prove that flat free boundaries of solutions of the inhomogeneous one-phase Stefan problem are C^{1,\alpha} . The method consists of employing a hodograph transform and deriving the regularity via a linearization technique, following the approach introduced by De Silva, Forcillo, and Savin in [ 7 ] .

arxiv-2405-18695.title: Data-Efficient Approach to Humanoid Control via Fine-Tuning a Pre-Trained GPT on Action Data
arxiv-2405-18695.creator: Siddharth Padmanabhan, Kazuki Miyazawa, Takato Horii, Takayuki Nagai
arxiv-2405-18695.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Siddharth Padmanabhan, Kazuki Miyazawa, Takato Horii, Takayuki Nagai. There are several challenges in developing a model for multi-tasking humanoid control. Reinforcement learning and imitation learning approaches are quite popular in this domain. However, there is a trade-off between the two. Reinforcement learning is not the best option for training a humanoid to perform multiple behaviors due to training time and model size, and imitation learning using kinematics data alone is not appropriate to realize the actual physics of the motion.

arxiv-2407-00854.title: Effects of Internal Resonance and Damping on Koopman Modes
arxiv-2407-00854.creator: Rahul Das, Anil K Bajaj, Sayan Gupta
arxiv-2407-00854.description: Abstract This study investigates the nonlinear normal modes (NNMs) of a system comprising of two coupled Duffing oscillators, with one oscillator being grounded and with the coupling being both linear and nonlinear. The study utilizes the eigenfunctions of the Koopman operator and validates their connection with the Shaw-Piere invariant manifold framework for NNMs.

arxiv-2503-04451.title: Privacy Preserving and Robust Aggregation for Cross-Silo Federated Learning in Non-IID Settings Conference: ; printacmref=false,printccs=false,printfolios=true
arxiv-2503-04451.creator: Marco Arazzi, Mert Cihangiroglu, Antonino Nocera
arxiv-2503-04451.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Marco Arazzi, Mert Cihangiroglu, Antonino Nocera. Federated Averaging remains the most widely used aggregation strategy in federated learning due to its simplicity and scalability. However, its performance degrades significantly in non-IID data settings, where client distributions are highly imbalanced or skewed. Additionally, it relies on clients transmitting metadata, specifically the number of training samples, which introduces privacy risks and may conflict with regulatory frameworks like the European GDPR.

arxiv-2507-03821.title: Experimental Investigation of Optical Processing With Spatial Light Modulation
arxiv-2507-03821.creator: M. G. Damaceno, A. Mucherino, R. Medeiros de Araújo, P. H. Souto Ribeiro, N. Rubiano da Silva
arxiv-2507-03821.description: Abstract The growing demand for real-time data processing in applications such as neural networks and embedded control systems has spurred the search for faster, more efficient alternatives to traditional electronic systems. In response, we experimentally investigate an optical processing scheme that encodes information in the transverse wavefront of light fields using spatial light modulators.
